- **A virtual filesystem over every source.**"},{"id":"p8s3","text":" S3, Google Drive, Slack, Gmail, Redis and the rest mount side by side under one root, so an agent r"},{"id":"p8s4","text":"eaches all of them through a unified interface with the unix tools it already knows, like `ls`, `gre"},{"id":"p8s5","text":"p`, `find` and `jq`.

- **Routed, dynamic runtimes.** Python, JavaScript and any other command can be sent to"},{"id":"p8s9","text":" a configured runtime, in process, sandboxed or remote, which decouples computation from storage and"},{"id":"p8s10","text":" lets either change without touching the other.

- **Lightweight by design.** A workspace, the virtual terminal itsel"},{"id":"p8s13","text":"f, takes about 100 KB of memory and each new session about 10 KB, so one process serves many agents "},{"id":"p8s14","text":"without a container or VM per agent.
- **Profiles designed for agents.** `allow`, `ask` and `deny` g"},{"id":"p8s15","text":"overn commands and CLIs, while `hide` and `show` govern files and folders, so a hidden path is not m"},{"id":"p8s16","text":"erely unreadable but absent from the filesystem the agent sees.
- **A scriptable policy engine.** A "},{"id":"p8s17","text":"policy script can prohibit any dangerous action before it runs, and the same stack gates every VFS o"},{"id":"p8s18","text":"p and session write, so neither a file nor an environment variable leaks.
